# OpenType feature settings

Source: usvg 0.47.0, original crates.io archive SHA-256 `d46cf96c5f498d36b7a9693bc6a7075c0bb9303189d61b2249b0dc3d309c07de`. `UPSTREAM.json` records the original source checksums and published Git revision. Original dual MIT/Apache-2.0 licenses and copyright notices are retained.

The upstream parser recognizes the property name `font-feature-settings` but never passes its values to Rustybuzz. Consequently standard SVG small caps, alternate glyphs and numeric features disagree with native text using the same font. The correction parses inherited CSS feature tags/values, keeps them in the font style/cache key, passes them to the existing shaper and fallback faces, and writes them when text is preserved. Explicit feature settings follow higher-level small-cap/kerning defaults. Invalid declarations inherit, while `normal`/`initial` reset. Unicode content, original font data, variation settings, glyph geometry, paint and the compositor stay on their existing routes. No package or dependency version changes.

The public in-memory laid-out span also exposes the existing resolved letter spacing, baseline shift and kerning flag. The native SVG inspector reads those values alongside the existing font size and actual glyph transform instead of displaying outer-font defaults. They do not alter shaping, SVG syntax, serialization or font data.

Nested `textLength` is resolved at its owning text element instead of being discarded by an intervening tspan or independently repeated for each paint/font span. Within a text chunk, scopes share their length budget, explicit child scopes are retained, and spacing/glyph advances follow the resolved length without scaling a range's accumulated pen position. This also makes the native inspector's measured horizontal scale reflect the actual rendered glyph transform. Independent browser cases cover parent, mixed-font, explicit-child and spacing-only groups. Cross-chunk length scopes remain a separate open renderer case.

The length budget includes the span's terminal letter spacing when it participates in a larger chunk; excluding it enlarged glyphs and displaced following text in the actual Chromium comparison. The final whole-chunk letter gap is already removed by the existing spacing pass. Exported native outline-based text requests `geometricPrecision` while retaining explicit source rendering hints. Native and independent-browser failures remain separate until the corrected output is verified.

An explicit nonzero character offset or rotation disables optional ligatures only around that position. The same full-context Rustybuzz shaping and fallback faces remain in use; required shaping and unaffected ligatures are retained. This lets an editable pair offset reach an interior character instead of being discarded inside a combined glyph. The offset arrays, Unicode, font programs and SVG syntax are unchanged.
